name: js-base64
instruction: Implement base64.js (CommonJS): module.exports = { encode, decode }. encode(str) returns the standard base64 of the string's UTF-8 bytes, with '=' padding. decode(b64) is the exact inverse and returns the original string. You must NOT use Buffer, atob, btoa, or TextEncoder/TextDecoder - do the UTF-8 and base64 conversion yourself. decode throws an Error on a string whose length is not a multiple of 4, on characters outside the base64 alphabet, and on misplaced padding.
